articleTitle: Security Management Education and Training of Critical Infrastructure Sectors’ Experts
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The article was solved by using the methods with an emphasis on the applied methodological approach to tackling the issue within the concepts of the security sector, personal security, emerging management theories concerning security risks and simulation technologies. The results could secure the protected interests of the state as strategic object for the security sciences that exploring reality through unique research areas, which are characterized by the selected objects of research and application of relevant theoretical and methodological approaches to the field of study. Our findings and conclusion can affect other theoretical and practical direction of research on the quality of education of security personnel for the critical infrastructure sectors to which our Transport sector is an important part too.

articleTitle: Continual Monitoring of Precision of Aerial Transport Objects
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: In accordance with the future aims, when these aerial transport objects (ATO) could fly in a selected corridor, it is also important to simulate states based on the status monitoring of dangerous situated in the complex environmental condition of the Slovak Republic (SR). With due regard to the orography of the territory, it is important to locate residual areas, where there is no possibility of their telemetric control. In the given issue, however, it is also necessary to take into account the legal framework representing a supplementary control function of maintaining flight safety of air traffic control in compliance with the ATM policies. The set-up of functional efficiency of controlling the flight of such an ATO in a complex area must be stable. In the article, stability is presented by error analysis at given lateral deviations after the ATO has switched into autonomous flight mode. Due to the errors caused by the external environment, the ATO must perform a precise flight into the area and achieve the success of the flight mission. For example, it may involve a flight into mountain territories, where it is important to secure the patient s status or the person under threat. The laboriousness of solution of such flights in a limited mountain terrain is divided into files of intelligent autonomous ports (Sky Control Object Power Environment - SCOPE). The task is to cover the residual areas for minimizing the time of rescuing persons present in the active corridors taking into account the probability of environmental change. Analysis in the article is the fundamental navigational task of flying in the corridor itself in a precise navigation mode of autonomous flight, while presuming the possibility of error occurrence of the Navigation Ergatic Complex (NEC), the element of which are made up of an inertial navigation system, Doppler sensor of speed and drift angle carried on an unmanned aerial vehicle.

articleTitle: Airport integrated operational center
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: An important aspect at the airport is its safety and security. As part of ensuring safety and security at the airport, individual forces must work together at tactical and operational level. One of the modern ways to improve safety and security can be to unify dispatching centers into one operating center. Verification of the functionality of an operating center can be a form of screening exercise. In the airport area, exercises are very demanding, not only in terms of organization, personnel and technical, but above all financially. The first part of article shows possible distribution of the airport forces in one integrated operational center. In the second part article points on simulations as a teaching methods and outlines the possibility of using simulations to perform an exercise at the airport.

articleTitle: Wizz Air cancels the base in Košice despite a minimum of 80% occupancy of flights to four destinations
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The following topics are dealt with: airports; jet engines; transportation; aerospace industry; autonomous aerial vehicles; aircraft; aircraft control; optimisation; air traffic control; blades.

articleTitle: Possible Detection of Multirotor UAVs Based on Disturbances in Magnetic Field
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The number of unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) incidents in the world is increasing, because it is not difficult to buy multirotor UAVs that are inexpensive and technologically well equipped. This is the reason why the development of detection systems gains importance. Radar systems and specific frequencies detectors have their limitations, so it is necessary to develop different sensing methods. The presented paper deals with the possible lowrange method to detect electric-powered multirotor UAVs based on the low frequency magnetic fields generated around them. The results of the realized experiments with magnetic field sensors show that the UAV creates measurable magnetic fields disturbances that could be used as an intrusion indicator.

articleTitle: Aeronautical Composite Construction Monitoring by Magnetic Microwires
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: the composite materials are more often used materials in aerospace industry. The defectoscopy of these materials are critical for their application in structural parts of constructions. Presented paper describes the simulation - experimental verification of contactless tensile stress measurement method. The glass fibre composite I-beam was prepared for experimental verification. The same beam was modelled and simulated in ANSYS to compare with experimental results. The simulation and experimental results are presented in the paper.

articleTitle: The follow-up on the Free Route Airspace Implementation in Slovakia with the proposed optimization model
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: This contribution is a free continuation of work FRABRA-Free Route Slovakia. The base of the concept FRABRA is the transition from current Air Traffic Services (ATS) Routes Network to Free Routes Operations in Slovak airspace. The main aim of this work is to define the content, inputs, and resources of the future work for FRA implementation in Slovakia with the proposed optimization model. The work also provides a general guide for researchers to apply current technologies, as Kopernio to search for appropriate resources related to their area of research.

articleTitle: Analysis of Point-to-Point versus Hub-and-Spoke airline networks
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The article deals with the issue of networking of air carriers. It compares two basic Point-to-Point and Hub-and-Spoke types. It presents their characteristics, describes their pros and cons, networking methodology, calculation of network coverage and provides a graphical representation. It focuses primarily on the operational and economic aspects of both models. The Point-to-Point system is currently applied by low-cost carries and the Hub-and-Spoke model of full-service carries.

articleTitle: Automatic Detection of Flight Maneuvers with the Use of Density-based Clustering Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Ever-changing situation in the aviation demands a change in flight training programs that would reflect present needs and threats in contrary to the traditional training that didn't changed much for decades. Therefore, new alternative training concepts have been developed that cover these needs. However, these concepts do not apply to initial training which seem to be a crucial phase of a pilot training. Thus, the aim was to create a software solution that would identify individual flight maneuvers and evaluate them so that the overall evaluation would be done by considering objective evaluation and flight instructors' subjective expertise. A study was done with strictly given flight schedules. For the purpose of automatic maneuver detection, density-based spatial clustering of applications with noise - DBSCAN clustering algorithm was used, which could determine maneuvers and thus exclude the noise from clusters of maneuvers. The results indicate that the proposed solution was able to identify the prescribed maneuvers with high sensitivity. The solution could be extended in the future to identify all flight maneuvers considering as many parameters from flight data recorder as possible and thus carry out complete objectively based pilot performance evaluation.

articleTitle: Current Status of Cyber Security in the Surveillance Data Processing Systems in Europe
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The objective of this paper is to present a comprehensive status of cyber security challenges in surveillance data networks. The cyber security is a major concern of current Air Traffic Systems. It is mandated by European Union as well as national law. Also, it can be used as a first reading to have a global overview of network security issues, challenges and potential solutions in surveillance networks.

articleTitle: The Simulation of Fire and Rescue Services Operations by Airplane Accidents
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: When we talk about airplane accidents, we can admit their specific features supported by an individuality in all cases. It is always very important that all fire and rescue service unites must cooperate effectively in order to minimalize crisis situations impact. Among others, firefighting services play a significant role in a case of airplane crashes. The Ministry of the Interior of The Czech Republic assigned a project dedicated to firefighter’s complex educational process. This project deals with different methods of firefighter’s trainings and such simulators during lifesaving initiatives. The theoretical and practical research approaches were chosen for running this project. An appointed project team suggested certain steps, achievements and research procedures for creating a supportive training and also practical (on the spot useable) software for fire and rescue teams. The simulation software must respond to current legal requirements, technical specifications and airplanes specific technical standards. The above mentioned must guarantee the research objective, as much natural as possible, to real emergency situations. Emergency situations can happen not only within airport boarders but also at any other places. Regarding this, our software has been dedicated to all organizational forms of fire and rescue services either airport, county or volunteer ones.

articleTitle: Modeling of the Flight Trajectory of Flying Objects
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: In this paper, we describe a modeling approach for simulation of motion of flying objects. Such model can be used to examine the accuracy and resistance of radio-navigation systems against interference. The design of the simulation model is based on a mathematical description of the motion of a flying object in a geocentric coordinate system (ECEF - Earth - Centered, Earth - Fixed). The flight trajectory of flying objects consists of a straight section and two turns. We present the process of transforming the coordinates of the local motion of the flying object into a geocentric coordinate system in the topocentric coordinate system. We determined the initial coordinates of the flying objects (FO) from the real flight situation from flightradar24. The computer simulation was performed in the Matlab programming environment.

articleTitle: The concept of an air driven propeller as a thruster for special use
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Propellers are very often used to produce necessary thrust for propelling aircraft especially for low speed flights. It is because of its higher propulsion efficiency in comparison with jet engines at these low speeds. This work describes conceptual design of a self-driven propeller, where the energy needed for its rotational movement is supplied only by compressed air. Such propelling device could be very beneficial for a lot of reasons, e.g. lightweight design, high power, improved airflow on the surfaces of propeller blade airfoils, lower aerodynamic drag force. This study also reveal some disadvantages connected with low efficiency of jet flow used for driving the propeller. Future design improvements are also described at the end of this paper.

articleTitle: IMU Accelerometer and Magnetometer Calibration Using Spectral Analysis
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The presented paper deals with the calibration methodology based on the spectral analysis. One of the advantages of the methodology is that for the accelerometers and magnetometers which are a part of the inertial measurement unit (IMU) only one calibration experiment is required. The methodology is based on the sensor rotation around one of three sensitivity axes placed perpendicularly to the plane of the vector of gravity. The positioning of the sensors can be performed stepwise but also continuously because there is no requirement for the assignment of samples to the particular degrees of the sensor rotation.

articleTitle: Is it Possible to Use the Experimental Identification Based on the Transition Characteristics for Micro Turbo Compressor Engines?
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Experimental identification as one of the possibilities of creating mathematical models of complex systems is a fast, simple and easy-to-use methodology. Even with a low percentage of knowledge of the modelled object (functionality, internal bonds, etc.) it is possible to obtain a mathematical model with high quality - similarity - verification. The disadvantage of experimental identification is the necessary existence of a functional complex system and a measuring - sensing apparatus. The Laboratory of intelligent control systems of aircraft engines has four full-featured functional systems - small and micro turbo compressor aviation jet engines. Experimental identification of small jet engines based on the measured transition characteristic is being researched using these engines. The question and topic of this article is to verify the possibilities and ways of creating mathematical models by experimental identification based on the acquired - measured transition characteristics for the smallest category of aircraft engines - micro turbo-compressor jet engine and evaluate obtained simulation models of different complexity.

articleTitle: Potential Uses of a New Type of Antenna in Aviation
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The article is dealing with the theory of Crossed Field Antenna-CFA. This type was patented recently and sees its practical application particularly in area of long and medium waves. A brief theoretical analysis of the principle of radiation of this new type of antenna, which is not wave dependent to its physical dimensions, is present in this article. The independence on waves of the current CFA s enables substantial reduction of mechanical dimensions for medium wave (MW) antennas. Thereby, the dimensions of MW antennas reduces from hundreds of meters to structures measuring only several meters without affecting their electrical parameters-like power, impedance and radiation. The article is presenting a proposal and an analysis regarding the potentials in using CFA in high frequency (HF) and very high frequency (VHF) frequency bands. From this point of view, reducing the size of the airborne communication antennas is among the long-term goals of the authors research conducted at the educational institute.

articleTitle: Methodology for Justification of Aviation Safety Investments
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Investment into safety is often seen as cost with little benefit; an obligation to meet standards rather than effort to truly improve on safety. Aviation industry of today already achieved excellent safety record and so it is hard to justify such investment in apparently resilient system. This study works with the assumption that safety and overall efficiency of operations are dependent. It analyzes data from safety occurrences in the aviation industry and provides mapping to relevant costs, both considering the remedy and possible prevention. It further provides base methodology for evaluation of current safety investments in the industry. In conclusion, the significant difference between costs related to remedy and prevention is used to justify trial of new technologies and measures to further improve on safety.

articleTitle: Basic Thermal Field Analysis of a Small Turbo-Jet Engine
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Information about temperature distribution in the thermal field can serve as one of the major parameters for turbojet engine diagnostics and can contribute to extended technical lifetime of the engine. The aim of the submitted paper is to perform a basic analysis of the thermal field distribution during various operational modes of a small turbojet engine. As the object for thermal field investigation, a small turbojet engine iSTC-21v, installed in a laboratory, was used. The thermal field has been captured by a thermographic camera. The article presents an analysis of temperature distribution in various nodes of the small turbojet engine, defining critical parts of the engine during its operation, which can be further analyzed for diagnostic purposes. It is expected that this analysis can also be applicable for high power jet engines.

articleTitle: Magnetic Materials for Small Magnetic Sensors and Airport Detectors
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Devices and machines used for airport security purposes use technologies from many different fields. Generally metal detectors are used to ensure security at the airport entrance areas. Magnetic sensors can be candidates to the optimal operation of the magnetic security gates or magnetic handheld detectors. In our work we analyze the physical properties of amorphous magnetic materials, exhibiting the giant magneto-impedance effect, suitable for use in magnetic field sensors.

articleTitle: Virtual Prototyping and Additive Manufacturing of a Vaned Diffuser for a Research Jet Engine
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Advanced methods can significantly reduce costs and time-to-market of new designs. This can be utilized in aviation industry including gas turbine units. The present paper focuses on two important aspects: virtual prototyping using computational fluid dynamics and additive manufacturing. These approaches have been utilized on the micro turbojet engine in the Laboratory of Department of Aeronautics, Naval Architecture and Railway Vehicles (DANAR) of Budapest University of Technology and Economics in order to investigate the stator vanes of the compressor stage. The paper describes the optimization process including numerical aspects and the experiments with an additive manufactured vane assembly.

articleTitle: Helicopter emergency medical services response time in the Central European Region
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: This article deals with helicopter emergency medical services in Slovak Republic, Czech Republic, Poland and Hungary. The article analyses and gives a comparison of effectiveness of the helicopter emergency medical services (HEMS) in different countries in terms of the services response time. Some ideal allocation of the helicopter emergency medical services in Slovak Republic was proposed in the conclusion of the article.

articleTitle: Investigation of Production Flaws in Thin Solid Carbon Laminates by Using Ultrasonic Phased Array Method
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Composites are used in wide variety of markets, including aerospace, architecture, automotive, military, etc.. Along with increased use of composites, multiple Non-Destructive Testing (NDT) methods have been further developed specifically for inspecting them. Among them one can single out Ultrasonic Phased Arrays. Research described in this article focuses on the use of UT PA for production flaw investigation on an aileron. Examined part was made of up to 16 layers of BAER 3068 epoxy carbon prepreg. Investigation was done by using tap test, conventional ultrasonic measurement and phased array methods. Phased array method allowed us to thoroughly check the affected specimen and confirm the presence of production flaw in the form of epoxy resin buildup. Results show how effective this method can be and present its advantages over traditional UT inspections.

articleTitle: An aerial survey on apses of Catholic churches in Székesfehérvár
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The aim of the work is to survey and create a 3D model of the apses of Catholic churches in Székesfehérvár. Székesfehérvár is the ancientcapital of Hungary for 500 years and has several old and rather new Catholic churches. Till now two churches have been examined. As the apses generally have a great height it seemed to be easier to use UAV to make photographs in order to create a comprehensive view and a 3D model of these inner areas. As the GPS was not available inside, a more careful flight was made during the process. The results were 3D models and videos made of photographs. Our future plan is to fly inside the other churches and to make a free access to these materials. They will also be used for educational purposes.

articleTitle: Aero-engine manufacturer - planning
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: This paper highlights operations and supply problem in area aero-engine manufacturer planning. Research show inconsistent quality, extended lead times, economic changes and limited labor supply pose the greatest threat to aero-engine manufacturer posistion.

articleTitle: Stability of a Hovering Coleoptere
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Single rotor vertical take-off and landing (VTOL) unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) is described. Severaldifferences in comparison to multirotor UAV have to be solved to handle succesfull flight. Geometry, acting forces and moments are investigated with goal to keep stable hovering. Stabilization system is recommended for freeing operators attention to the main flight task.

articleTitle: Implement policies and processes to increase the level of security of the multi-tier logistics chain
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The level of security of the distribution chain products depends on many external factors. The stability is the most important factors affected the distribution chain include theft, contamination, damage or destruction. At present, there is a constantly high threat of terrorist attacks or leadership asymmetric wars in the context of the global war on terror are growing threats related to the smuggling of weapons or components needed to produce weapons of mass destruction. Vulnerability of air operations puts pressure on international organizations, transnational clusters and national governments to take measures to increase the safety of all actors in the distribution chain. Designers and chain managers face constant pressure to increase the level of distribution network security based on the need to carry out policies and regulations at all levels. Available scientific literature offers different statistics on the success of the measures taken and the directives adopted to increase security and safety of air operations. The presented article provides an overview of the adopted security measures in the Czech Republic's air operations, identifying at the same time the weak spots of the distribution chain and offering a summary of measures to increase the level of stability of the distribution chain. Recommendations are the first analysis of the building projects "Using Crisis Management Tools to Evaluate Safety and Quality or Resilience, Supply Chain of Small Airports", "Using Crisis Management Tools and Modern Technologies to Increase the Protection and Resilience of Military Aviation Basis" and "Improving Safety and Crisis airport management via sensor networks" [31]. The authors used scientific methods combinations in the process of processing the article, such as literary search, structured interviews, historical comparison methods, and gathering, analysis and deduction, and induction in classifying findings.

articleTitle: Local Modular Departure Control System for Airports
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The authors of the contribution are submitting the actual results of a design and implementation of a modular and local departure control system of the IMARA system with a primary focus on low-cost airlines. The reader has presented an explanation of the services and functions currently realized solutions for check-in and gate clients at airport terminals along with the methods and technologies used for the implementation of the individual software modules of the system. The introduced system enables variable configurations of the separate workplaces employed at passenger check-in and airplane boarding. Its variability makes it possible to allocate workplaces either by the plan of operation or the actual needs of the passenger handling company. The solution realized by the authors can also be used for simulation of real operation when dealing with both the passenger and baggage handling processes.

articleTitle: Risk Management in the Process of Aircraft Ground Handling
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The article deals with the issue of risk management and opportunities in the context of the ISO 31000 standard. The methodology of applying the requirements of the standard in question is applied to the aircraft handling process. As a result, on the basis of the defined process, the creation of a register of stakeholders, a register of internal and external impacts, and a register of risks and opportunities. This process applied to the aircraft clearance process can be devoted to any process in accordance with the organization's requirements for applying risk management and opportunities.

articleTitle: A Distributed Quadratic Generation Scheduling Optimization and Reserve Allocation Approach Based on the Decomposition of Generation Characteristics
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The operation with the limited resources requires optimization. Also in an island mode on board energy system or in the large power system the optimal power generation distribution between the operating units is crucial for increase the success of the mission or for the protection of the environment or decrease the costs. A method for generator scheduling and simultaneous allocation of reserves is proposed in this article. Based on the decomposition and piecewise linear approximation of generation characteristics, we formulate the optimization framework in a distributed manner, making the utilization of parallel computing power possible. We define a finite number of operation modes for each generator, and analyze the feasibility and resulting cost of their possible combinations. Secondary and tertiary reserves are also allocated in the process. A simple heuristic is introduced to reduce the number of operating profiles taken into account.

articleTitle: Development of a Micro-Turbojet Test Rig for Investigating Effects of Alternative Fuel
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: The goal of the present paper is to describe a turbojet test bench dedicated to investigate the effect of alternative fuels on the operational parameters of a gas turbine engine. Aviation uses significant amounts of fuel including commercial as well as military applications. Due to environment concerns and possible shortage of fossil fuel sources, the engine developers have considered alternative fuels already from the 1980's. Though the above mentioned problems constantly emerge nowadays there is no mature technology that could be used widely. Therefore intensive research of the problem is still up-to-date. The main intent of the authors is to focus on the establishment of a data acquisition system, which can reveal the differences in operational parameters of the turbojet engine if the type of fuel is changed.

articleTitle: Air Transport Services a Monopoly in Air Navigation Services
publicationTitle: 2018 XIII International Scientific Conference - New Trends in Aviation Development (NTAD)
abstract: Air traffic over the Czech Republic has continued to grow in recent years. The Air Navigation Services of the Czech Republic, as the company responsible for the safety of air navigation in the Czech Republic, plays in it a vital role. The purpose of this paper is to elaborate the economic performance of Air Navigation Services of the Czech Republic (ANS CR) in the context of regulation in this sector to evaluate its basic parameters of performance in the context of its status as a monopoly, and to assess its competitiveness in terms of the objectives of SES legislation. With the exception of advertising and product differentiation, the mission of the company gives it the character of a monopoly in the air navigation services market. The elaboration of this paper is based in particular on the methods used in describing the mission and activities of the company, as well as on the method of comparative analysis in evaluating the development of the performance indicators of the company. Economic globalization has allowed the company to improve its position considerably among other European partners. This has been mainly due to the growth of tourism, which can be traced to the emergence of low-cost airlines and a drop in fares in general. The deployment of wide-body passenger airliners has been another force in the growth of the economic performance of ANS CR. These factors suggest further, positive developments for the company in the future.
